subject: general
question: In 2005, ASHA was instituted by the Government of India's Ministry of Health and Family Welfare as a part of the National Rural Health Mission. What is the full form of 'ASHA'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Accredited Social Health Activist**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Accredited Social Health Activist** (ASHA) was instituted by the Government of India's Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in 2005.
 
• ASHA is a part of the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM), which aims to provide effective healthcare in rural areas.
 
• ASHAs are community health workers instituted by the government to act as an interface between the community and the public health system.
 
• Their primary role includes promoting health education, increasing access to health services, and addressing social determinants of health.
 
• ASHA workers are trained to work as an intermediary between the health system and the rural population, ensuring that rural inhabitants receive adequate healthcare services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) was launched in April 2005 to improve health care delivery across rural India.
 
• ASHA workers are selected from the village itself and are accountable to it, making them a crucial part of the community's healthcare delivery system.
 
• They are trained to provide information and help people access the benefits of various health schemes offered by the government.
 
• ASHA workers also play a vital role in promoting immunization, maternal health, child health, and family planning services.
 
• They act as a link between the rural population and the health services, ensuring that the benefits of health schemes reach the rural population effectively.
